title: CPU-Z — What CPU-Z does
description: CPU-Z by CPUID is the classic free utility that catalogs the processor, motherboard, memory, and graphics of any PC on tabbed pages. Reviewers, overclockers, and second-hand buyers have trusted its read-only reports for over two decades.

title: CPU-Z — Installing CPU-Z
description: CPU-Z comes as an installer or a portable ZIP with 32- and 64-bit builds, and it starts reporting the moment it opens. It reads hardware registers directly, so it works even on machines with no drivers installed yet.

title: CPU-Z — Clocks and multiplier
description: Core speed is the bus speed times the multiplier, and CPU-Z shows all three live so you can watch boost behavior in real time. A multiplier of 42 on a 100 MHz bus is 4,200 MHz, and the demo recomputes it to prove the arithmetic.

title: CPU-Z — The Caches tab
description: The Caches tab breaks down L1, L2, and L3 by size, associativity, and descriptor, showing how much fast memory sits next to each core. Large shared L3 — like the 7800X3D's stacked 96 MB — is exactly what makes some chips fly in games.

title: CPU-Z — Memory timings
description: The timings table lists CAS latency and the secondary timings the board actually trained, like 30-38-38-96 at DDR5-6000. Lower first numbers at the same frequency mean a snappier kit, and the command rate (1T/2T) sits at the end.

title: CPU-Z — Bench tab
description: The Bench tab runs CPU-Z's own single- and multi-thread benchmark and compares the result against a reference database. The multi-to-single ratio reveals scaling: eight full cores should land near eight times the single-thread score.
